Where to Stay in Uttaradit?

heroSub: 11 hand-picked Uttaradit hotels across every budget — from a town-centre hotel with a pool and a suburban boutique to a wooden guesthouse in the old town of Laplae and a riverside stay by Sirikit Dam. Covering the town centre, Laplae and the Tha Pla–Sirikit Dam side. From roughly ฿400–1,200/night.
introH2: 🏯 Why does choosing the right area in Uttaradit matter so much?
introHtml: Uttaradit is a stopover town on the northern route that many people stay in for a single night — but it actually has sights spread across several areas. Stays fall into three sides with very different feels — the town centre has the clock tower, the Phraya Phichai Dab Hak monument, the railway station and a mall, ideal if you arrive by train or don't have a car; the old town of Laplae sits about 20 minutes away, with old wooden houses, museums and famous Laplae noodles; and the Tha Pla–Sirikit Dam side is around 45–60 minutes out, handy for the dam and the Nan River. Many people book without checking the area and end up driving back and forth all day. This guide rounds up 11 hand-picked Uttaradit hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Uttaradit has no metro and no commercial airport — but its trump card is that the northern-line railway station sits in the town centre, with every Bangkok–Chiang Mai train stopping here, so many people arrive by train and walk or take a short ride to their hotel. Pick by your itinerary: the town centre (Tha It–Tha Sao) is near the station, the clock tower, the mall and the markets, best if you don't have a car; the old town of Laplae (Si Phanom Mat) lets you walk to the old town gate, museums and Laplae noodle shops; and Tha Pla–Sirikit Dam is about 45–60 minutes from town, handy for the dam and a riverside stay on the Nan River. Almost every hotel has free parking, so they suit self-drivers well.

entries.name: Seeharaj Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Boromat Rd · Tha It · town centre
tags: 🚶 Town centre · walk to the mall
entries.addr: Boromat Rd, Tha It, Mueang Uttaradit
entries.storyHtml: Seeharaj is the town-centre midrange hotel that best balances a solid score with a healthy review count — 8.6 from 78 reviews. It sits on Boromat Road in the heart of town, a two-minute walk from Friday department store and close to the railway and bus stations. Its standout is a swimming pool, rare in this price bracket in Uttaradit; the Deluxe and Suite rooms are more recently refreshed, making it a fit for both leisure and business trips.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, go for a Deluxe Room — it has been refreshed more recently and is noticeably larger and better-kept than the Superior.

Has a swimming pool, rare at this price
Town-centre location, walk to the mall and markets
Near the railway and bus stations, good without a car
cons: The older Superior rooms are dated next to the refreshed ones

entries.name: Barista Hotel
entries.revCount: 105 reviews · the most in this guide
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Sao · suburbs · near Rajabhat Uni
entries.storyHtml: Barista Hotel is the boutique hotel with the most reviews in this guide — 105, scoring 8.3. Its standout is an on-site cafe for a morning coffee, with clean, boutique-styled rooms from just ฿650. It sits in the Tha Sao suburb near Uttaradit Rajabhat University, about a 10-minute drive into town — a fit for self-drivers who want a stay with a bit of style at a friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget allows, take a Deluxe with a balcony — you can sip a coffee from the hotel's own cafe out there in the morning.

entries.name: ARAYA HOTEL
entries.addr: Phitsanulok-Den Chai Rd, Khung Taphao, Mueang Uttaradit
entries.storyHtml: ARAYA HOTEL is a villa-style hotel with a pool and rooms that are larger than the price suggests, scoring 8.3 from 81 reviews. The rooms are villas of around 36 sqm with private balconies, starting at just ฿600, while the Luxury and Boutique Villa rooms are more recently renovated. It sits on the Phitsanulok-Den Chai road on the Khung Taphao side, about a 10-minute drive into town — a fit for self-drivers wanting a large room with a pool at a friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The renovated Luxury Room is in noticeably better shape than the Standard Villa for only a few hundred baht more — worth it.

entries.name: Areena Resort and Hotel Uttaradit
entries.storyHtml: Areena Resort is the small resort with the highest review score among the hotels in this guide — 8.8 (from 17 reviews). It's a cluster of single-storey garden cottages with a quiet suburban feel and parking right at your door. Rooms start at just ฿490 and include breakfast, which is a strong deal. It's in the Tha It area, about a 10-minute drive into town — a fit for self-drivers who want a clean, quiet, budget-friendly stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Rooms are limited and the score is high, so it fills fast on long weekends — booking ahead pays off.

entries.storyHtml: Laplae Guesthouse is the old wooden-house stay in the old town of Laplae with the highest review score in this guide — 9.2 (from 14 reviews). Its draw is the nostalgic feel: rooms in an old wooden house with mosquito-net beds and vintage decor, within walking distance of the Laplae old town gate, the museums and the famous Laplae noodle shops. From just ฿500, it's a fit for anyone wanting to soak up old-town Laplae on foot.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: In Laplae, get up early for Laplae noodles and a walk through the old town gate before the heat — the guesthouse is right within walking distance.

entries.storyHtml: Baan Na Pasiri Resort is a riverside resort on the Nan River on the Tha Pla side, near Sirikit Dam, scoring 8.6 from 12 reviews. Its draw is riverside cottages with a relaxing waterside terrace, a small water playground for kids and breakfast included — a fit for families wanting a quiet riverside stay. It's about a 20-minute drive to Sirikit Dam, ideal for visiting the dam and the Nan River without driving back into town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For the full feel, choose a Nan River House with a riverside terrace — lovely to sit out by the water in the evening.

entries.name: Thaimit Resort
entries.storyHtml: Thaimit Resort is the well-reviewed budget resort (96 reviews) and the cheapest of the in-town stays, from just ฿400, scoring 8.0. Rooms are clean with a TV, fridge and hot water; some Deluxe rooms have a garden-facing balcony, and there's a Family Room for small families. It's in the Tha Sao area in town near Rajabhat University, about an 8-minute drive into the centre — a fit for budget travellers who just want a clean, cheap base.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: A little extra gets you a Deluxe Room with a garden-facing balcony — airier than the Standard for only a few hundred baht more.

entries.name: Sirikit Dam Guesthouse (EGAT)
entries.revCount: 64 reviews · inside the Sirikit Dam grounds
entries.addr: Sirikit Dam grounds, Tha Pla District, Uttaradit
entries.storyHtml: Sirikit Dam Guesthouse (run by EGAT) is the state-run guesthouse inside the Sirikit Dam grounds that lets you stay right by the reservoir, scoring 7.8 from 64 reviews. Its draw is the location inside the dam grounds — walking distance to the dam crest, the viewpoint and the public park, and near the reservoir cruise pier. Rooms are simple and clean, ranging from terraced rooms to a Nan riverside house — a fit for travellers set on visiting the dam who want to wake up to reservoir views.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The dam stay is state-run and very busy on long weekends, so contact them to book well ahead and check the conditions before you travel.

faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Uttaradit hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in in Uttaradit?
faq.a: It depends on your plans and whether you have a car. The town centre (Tha It–Tha Sao) is near the railway station, clock tower, mall and markets, best without a car (Seeharaj, Friday, Thaimit, Sunee, Barista). The old town of Laplae lets you walk to the old town gate and museums (Laplae Guesthouse). Tha Pla–Sirikit Dam is about 45–60 minutes from town, handy for the dam and a riverside stay on the Nan River (Baan Na Pasiri, Sirikit Dam Guesthouse).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Uttaradit hotels cost?
faq.a: Uttaradit is very affordable: budget 2-star stays start around ฿400–500 (Thaimit, Friday, Laplae Guesthouse, Areena); 3-star hotels and boutiques are around ฿600–850 (ARAYA, Barista, Sunee, RocKo, Seeharaj); and riverside resorts on the dam side start around ฿700–1,200 (Sirikit Dam Guesthouse, Baan Na Pasiri).

faq.q: ❓ Arriving by train — where can I stay within walking distance?
faq.a: Uttaradit has a northern-line railway station in the town centre, with every Bangkok–Chiang Mai train stopping here. Stays within walking distance or a short ride of the station are Friday Hotel (attached to the mall, in the centre) and Seeharaj Hotel (on Boromat Rd, near the station) — ideal if you arrive by train and want to walk to your hotel.

faq.q: ❓ Which Uttaradit hotels have a swimming pool?
faq.a: In this guide, the ones with a pool are Seeharaj Hotel (an in-town hotel with a pool) and ARAYA HOTEL (villas with a pool and spacious balcony rooms). Both are in town or the suburbs, from ฿600–850.

faq.q: ❓ Want to visit Sirikit Dam — where should I stay?
faq.a: If you're set on visiting Sirikit Dam and a reservoir cruise, stay on the Tha Pla side. Sirikit Dam Guesthouse (EGAT) ฿700 puts you inside the dam grounds, walking distance to the dam crest and pier. Baan Na Pasiri Resort ฿1,200 is a Nan River cottage stay about a 20-minute drive from the dam. Both are 45–60 minutes from town, so a car helps.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book an Uttaradit hotel?
faq.a: On ordinary weekdays, booking 1–2 weeks ahead is plenty, as Uttaradit isn't a crowded market. But on long weekends and holidays, small-room stays like Laplae Guesthouse and the Sirikit Dam stays fill fast, so book 2–4 weeks ahead or more.
